articles.title: From Paris to DC - why offices are being turned into apartments
articles.description: Office buildings with low occupancy rates are being transformed into flats.

It all sounds appealing, an upmarket flat in the west of Paris, but presently the space doesn't look like one at all.
That's because it's currently a corner of one floor of a nine-storey office building called Le Diamant, where 1,800 people work.

articles.title: Some under-25s should get fewer benefits, Milburn review to say
articles.description: The proposed radical overhaul of the welfare system would move under-25s off the main sickness benefits.
articles.summary: Some young people could see reductions to the benefits they are entitled to, under a radical overhaul of the system to be recommended by a government-commissioned review.
key_points: Alan Milburn's year-long report, which will be published on Tuesday, will recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, the Times reported , external .
Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, has been tasked by the government with helping reduce the one in eight 18- to 24-year-olds in the UK who are not in education, employment or training…
He said on Wednesday night that his plans would not be "pain-free" and would affect both existing and new claimants.

articles.title: Claude chatbot maker set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
articles.description: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.
articles.summary: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.
key_points: The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month.
It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times.
The huge valuation comes despite the company warning last month that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity".

key_points: Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.

However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.
